phases.summary: Read the Closure-1f source for RemoveUnusedVars.removeUnreferencedFunctionArgs. It contains three control points: the early global-removal guard that the original Defects4J Closure-1 fix added, a dedicated object-literal accessor exemption guard, and a trailing-formal strip loop that is bypassed when call-site modification is enabled.

Considered candidates that preserve the Closure-1 semantic family (unused function-argument removal producing an externally invalid function shape) while changing the trigger condition and the observable failure. The accessor exemption guard was selected because it is protected by a distinct repository invariant, is checked by the compiler's own AST validator, and leaves several concrete repository-grounded decoys live.
rejected_candidates: Re-weakening the global-removal guard: equivalent in location and near-equivalent in meaning to CLOSURE-1-L10-001, which already occupies that site.

Faulting NodeUtil.isGetOrSetKey directly: would move the gold into a widely shared AST helper, inflating blast radius and removing the helper-versus-caller discrimination that carries the strict depth.
Removing the exemption guard entirely: a coarser edit that deletes the evidence a solver needs to distinguish an absent protection from an inert one.

phases.summary: Reviewed against the strict rubric: not equivalent to the original Closure-1 bug (different guard, different trigger condition, different observable failure), not trivial (the failure names neither the gold class nor the gold method), not artificial (a one-token AST-navigation error is a realistic defect), deterministic, and testable by a single trigger.

One token changed: the accessor exemption guard now inspects the function node instead of its parent accessor key, making it unconditionally inert. One deterministic trigger added to IntegrationTest, deliberately placed outside the gold class's own test file to avoid naming the owner in the agent-visible file path.
Full gate executed by crflb-validate.sh/v1 in a single run; every figure in validation.json is captured output, not narrative.

Canonical package written with full-tree source hashes (916 files before and after, aggregate digest, exactly 2 modified), real captured failure output in trigger.stack_trace, and complete provenance including validator version and toolchain.

toolchain.test_runner: SingleMethodRunner/v1 over the checkout's own junit.jar

no_model_or_agent_used: No LLM, mini-swe-agent or fault-localization run was involved in constructing or validating this variant.
